FINDINGS:

FILES_EXAMINED:
- src/app/page.tsx:1-5 — trivial server component, renders `<MapstackApp />` only; no routing/tab structure exists at this level.
- src/components/MapstackApp.tsx:1-75 — the entire app shell. Single `useState` set (`active: ActiveLayer[]`, `selectedCityId`, `year`) held in this one client component; no context/reducer/router. One fixed layout (sidebar + map), no mode-switch or tab primitive anywhere.
- src/lib/datasets/types.ts:1-93 — the core `Dataset` interface plus its own design-rationale comment block, which explicitly names cross-dataset combination as deferred (see `combineDatasetValues` reference).
- src/lib/datasets/registry.ts:1-15 — flat `DATASETS: Dataset[]` array (`allergyDataset`, `crimeDataset`); adding a dataset means only implementing the interface and appending to this array — comment states no other file needs to change.
- src/lib/active-layers.ts:1-35 — `ActiveLayer {datasetId, layerId}` pair, `resolveActiveLayer`, `isSameLayer`, `activeLayerKey` — the only cross-dataset-aware plumbing that exists today, and it only supports independent stacked rendering, not correlation.
- src/lib/datasets/crime.ts:1-88 — concrete real dataset impl: percentile-ranked (`concern`, 0-100) per (`cityId`, `layerId`, `year`), backed by static JSON (`@data/crime.json`) generated from FBI Crime Data Explorer via a build-time script (`scripts/gen_crime_data.py`), with a `methodologyUrl` field mandated by the interface.
- src/components/CityDetailPanel.tsx:1-65 — per-city detail view; iterates `active` layers and calls each dataset's `getValue` independently — no combination/correlation logic; this is the closest existing surface to "show two datasets side-by-side for one city," but only for the single currently-selected city, not a shortlist.
- (grep only, not read) no hits anywhere in src/ for `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `URLSearchParams`, `useSearchParams`, or `cookie` — confirms zero persistence today.
- /Users/mdostal/Code/allergy-locator/src/lib/profiles.ts:1-47 (read in full) — the "saved-profile" pattern: `SavedProfile {id, name, sensitivities, savedAt}`, flat array under one `localStorage` key (`allergy-locator:saved-profiles`), CRUD via `getSavedProfiles`/`saveProfile`/`deleteProfile`/`renameProfile`, fail-open on corrupt JSON (returns `[]`, never throws), SSR-safe (`typeof window === "undefined"` guard).
- /Users/mdostal/Code/allergy-locator/src/lib/url-state.ts (grep only, ~193 lines) — companion pattern: encodes app state into a single query param (`s`), plus separate `compare`/`view` params (`COMPARE_IDS_PARAM`, `COMPARE_VIEW_PARAM`) so a "compare 2 profiles" view round-trips through the URL while the actual profile data stays in localStorage — comment explicitly frames this as "restore my own session on reload," not cross-device share.

PATTERNS_OBSERVED:
- Pattern: single flat registry array | File: src/lib/datasets/registry.ts | Detail: every dataset-aware component (AddLayerPanel, ActiveLayersList, MultiLayerMap, CityDetailPanel) is generic over `DATASETS`; a new capability that needs to enumerate/query all datasets can reuse this registry directly.
- Pattern: "higher = more concerning" 0-100 contract | File: src/lib/datasets/types.ts:38-42 | Detail: every dataset's `getValue` returns a value on one shared scale specifically so cross-dataset math (comparison, correlation, combination) is arithmetically valid without per-dataset renormalization — this is a designed-in enabler for the correlation/shortlist ask.
- Pattern: percentile framing is dataset-local and year-scoped | File: src/lib/datasets/crime.ts:16-20 | Detail: crime's `concern` is "percentile rank among that year's covered cities," not an absolute severity — comment warns this is NOT comparable across years or (implicitly) not directly comparable to allergy's climate-modeled percentile without care; any cross-dataset correlation feature must surface/respect this or risk a misleading "apples-to-apples" claim.
- Pattern: everything client-side, no backend | File: src/components/MapstackApp.tsx (all `"use client"`), consistent with allergy-locator's profiles.ts comment ("client-side only via localStorage, no accounts, no backend") | Detail: mapstack-us appears to be following the same static-first, no-backend posture as its predecessor — relevant constraint for import/save/feedback features.
- Pattern: saved-profile CRUD module, ported candidate | File: /Users/mdostal/Code/allergy-locator/src/lib/profiles.ts | Detail: small (46 lines), self-contained, SSR-safe, fail-open localStorage wrapper — directly adaptable for mapstack's "save settings" ask (would need a new key namespace and a shape matching `ActiveLayer[]`/year/etc. instead of `sensitivities`).
- Pattern: URL state as session-restore, not sharing | File: /Users/mdostal/Code/allergy-locator/src/lib/url-state.ts | Detail: separate concerns — localStorage owns durable saved data, URL params own "what am I looking at right now" (including a `compare` param for 2+ saved items) — a pattern directly reusable for a power-user shortlist/compare view.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Constraint: `Dataset.getValue` signature is `(cityId, layerId, context?) => DatasetLayerValue | null`, single dataset/single layer per call | Source: src/lib/datasets/types.ts:92 | Impact: there is no existing entry point that takes 2+ datasets and returns a joint/correlated result — any correlation feature needs new code, likely a new function/module (`combineDatasetValues`, referenced only in a comment, never implemented) sitting above the per-dataset `getValue` calls, not a change to the interface's core contract.
- Constraint: `Dataset` interface has no field for user-supplied/ad-hoc data | Source: src/lib/datasets/types.ts:70-93 | Impact: "import your own data" cannot slot in as a normal registry entry without deciding whether an imported CSV becomes (a) a fully synthesized object satisfying the `Dataset` interface at runtime (in-memory, not in `registry.ts`'s static array) or (b) a parallel, lighter-weight shape — this is an open design question, not a solved one.
- Constraint: `MapstackApp` holds all state as local `useState` in one component, no context/store | Source: src/components/MapstackApp.tsx:16-27 | Impact: introducing a second "tab"/"mode" means either lifting state up (to share `active`/`year`/`selectedCityId` between simple and power-user views) or duplicating/forking it — no existing seam (context, router, reducer) to plug a second mode into cleanly today.
- Constraint: zero routing — single page, no Next.js route segments beyond the root | Source: src/app/page.tsx, no other files under src/app/ besides layout.tsx | Impact: a "tab" most likely means client-side state (`activeTab` or similar) inside `MapstackApp`, or a new Next.js route (`/advanced`) — both are green-field, no precedent to follow in this repo.
- Constraint: static-first / no-backend architecture (data ships as bundled JSON, generated at build time via scripts) | Source: src/lib/datasets/crime.ts:1, `@data/crime.json` import; consistent with allergy-locator's localStorage-only comment | Impact: "save settings" and "feedback/comments" both need a client-only (localStorage) or external-service answer, since there's no app server/API route observed in this repo to build on.

RISKS:
- Severity: high | Risk: cross-dataset correlation risks becoming exactly the "black-box heuristic" the operator wants to avoid, because the codebase's own scores are NOT on a uniform statistical basis today (crime = year-scoped percentile rank; allergy = climate-model-derived score — see crime.ts:16-20) | Evidence: crime.ts comment explicitly flags its percentile is "not comparable across years," and by extension likely not naively comparable to a different dataset's 0-100 score without documenting what the correlation actually means statistically.
- Severity: medium | Risk: "ad-hoc imported dataset" may not cleanly satisfy the existing `Dataset` interface's mandatory fields (`methodologyUrl`, `availableYears`, transparent-sourcing convention) | Evidence: types.ts's own doc comment frames `methodologyUrl` as a MUST ("every dataset MUST document its sourcing/method/limitations") — a user-imported CSV has no methodology doc, creating friction against the stated "must stay transparent/sourced/cited" requirement for the new epic.
- Severity: medium | Risk: no persistence layer exists in mapstack-us today (confirmed via grep) — the allergy-locator pattern is a *reference*, not a shared dependency; porting it means re-implementing (copy/adapt), including re-deciding storage-key naming, schema versioning, and SSR-guard conventions from scratch | Evidence: grep of src/ returned zero hits for localStorage/URLSearchParams/cookie.
- Severity: low | Risk: "feedback/comments path" has no existing analog in either repo's grepped surface (no mail/API/form component found in this pass) | Evidence: absence — not verified by a deep dive, flagged as unanswered below.

UTILITIES_AVAILABLE:
- Utility: `DATASETS` / `getDataset(id)` | File: src/lib/datasets/registry.ts | Relevance: the natural enumeration point for any power-user UI that needs to list/pick from all available datasets at once (e.g., for a correlation matrix or shortlist builder).
- Utility: `resolveActiveLayer`, `isSameLayer`, `activeLayerKey` | File: src/lib/active-layers.ts | Relevance: existing helpers for working with (dataset, layer) pairs; a shortlist/correlation feature would likely need analogous helpers operating over city IDs × multiple ActiveLayers.
- Utility: `SavedProfile` CRUD pattern (`getSavedProfiles`, `saveProfile`, `deleteProfile`, `renameProfile`) | File: /Users/mdostal/Code/allergy-locator/src/lib/profiles.ts | Relevance: directly portable template for mapstack's "save settings" capability — needs adaptation from `sensitivities: Record<string,number>` to whatever a mapstack "saved view" shape becomes (active layers + year + maybe shortlist criteria).
- Utility: URL-state encode/decode + compare-params pattern | File: /Users/mdostal/Code/allergy-locator/src/lib/url-state.ts | Relevance: template for making a power-user "compare" or "shortlist" view shareable/restorable via URL without needing a backend.
- Utility: `CITY_BY_ID` city lookup map | File: src/components/CityDetailPanel.tsx:8 (built from `@data/cities.json`) | Relevance: existing indexed city list reusable for any shortlist-building UI needing to enumerate/search cities.

EXTERNAL_REFERENCES:
- Source: none consulted (pure internal/codebase-only research per scope) — Relevance: n/a — Key takeaway: n/a

UNANSWERED_QUESTIONS:
- Does allergy-locator's `ProfileCompare.tsx` / `ProfileOverlayMap.tsx` (found via grep, not read) contain a ranking/scoring UI pattern that's a closer analog to "shortlist of cities across unrelated segments" than plain profile-diffing? Out of scope for this pass per the instruction to only light-touch allergy-locator.
- Is there any existing CSV/file-import parsing utility anywhere in either repo (not grepped for in this pass) that "import your own data" could build on, or would that be entirely new?
- Does mapstack-us have any feedback/comments mechanism precedent at all (e.g., a GitHub-issues-link pattern, a mailto, a third-party widget) — not found in this pass, may need a dedicated look.
- What exact statistical treatment (if any) would make cross-dataset correlation defensible given the differing scales (percentile-rank vs. modeled score) — this is a design/definition question, not a code-location question, and stays with the design/planning stage, not research.

INCONSISTENCY_RISK_SIGNALS:
- Signal: hidden assumption | Where: src/lib/datasets/types.ts's 0-100 "higher = more concerning" shared-scale contract | Detail: the interface's own comment sells this as enabling one universal color ramp and (implicitly) cross-dataset math, but crime.ts's percentile-rank-per-year framing shows the 0-100 values are NOT actually commensurate across datasets/years today — a correlation feature built naively on top of `getValue()` alone would silently violate the "no black-box heuristics / stay transparent" requirement unless it explicitly surfaces each dataset's scoring methodology per comparison.
- Signal: unresolved tension | Where: types.ts comment line 26-30 ("cross-dataset combination is a separate, likely later concept -- see combineDatasetValues below for the narrow slice of that already built") vs. actual code | Detail: `combineDatasetValues` is referenced as if it exists ("already built") but a full-repo grep found zero implementation — the comment describes a function that was apparently planned/removed/never landed; anyone reading types.ts alone would believe partial cross-dataset combination logic already exists in the codebase, and it does not.
- Signal: vocabulary mismatch | Where: "tab" (operator's stated UI term) vs. codebase | Detail: no `Tab`, `tab`, `mode` component/hook/type exists anywhere in src/ — the epic's framing ("advanced power-user tab") presumes a UI primitive that must be built from zero, not extended from an existing (even hidden/unused) tab system.
- Signal: convention violation risk | Where: methodologyUrl-mandatory convention (types.ts:75-78) vs. "import your own data" ask | Detail: the codebase's own hard rule ("every dataset MUST document its sourcing/method/limitations") is structurally incompatible with a user pasting/uploading arbitrary data with no methodology doc — the epic's "avoid black-box heuristics / stay transparent" instruction and its "import your own data" instruction pull in different directions unless user-imported data is deliberately scoped as a different, clearly-labeled category (e.g., visually/contractually distinguished from vetted datasets) rather than shoehorned into the existing `Dataset` interface as-is.

VALIDATION NOTE:
  Checked: none — pure internal codebase research
  Source: codebase-only
  Confidence: high
  Findings: All three research questions were answered directly from primary source files (read in full for small/medium files: page.tsx, MapstackApp.tsx, types.ts, registry.ts, active-layers.ts, crime.ts, CityDetailPanel.tsx, allergy-locator's profiles.ts) plus targeted grep confirming absence of persistence/tab mechanisms in mapstack-us and presence of the saved-profile/url-state pattern in allergy-locator (file names and export surfaces only, per the light-touch instruction). No external library/API behavior was in scope for this research pass.
